This Indian "Standard (Second Revision) which is identical with ISO 9249:1997 `Earth-moving machine~ -- Engine test code -- Net powet issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Material Handling Systems and Equipment Sectional Committee and approval of the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1991. Present revision has been taken up to harmonize it with the latest version of ISO Standard. The text of the ISO Standard has been approved as suitable for publicationas an Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards. Indian Standard

EARTH-MOVING MACHINERY -- ENGINE TEST CODE -- NET POWER
( Second Revision)
1 Scope
This International Standard specifias a method for testing internal combwtion engines intended for propulsion of earth-moving machinery as defined in ISO 6165. It applies to evaluation of performance with a view, in particular, to presenting curves of power and specific fuel consumption at full load as a function of engine speed. The engines may ba naturally aspirated or pressure-charged. It applies to net powar assessment. This International Standard concerns internal combustion used earth-moving engines in machinery and included in one of the following categories: - reciprocating internal combustion engines (spark-ignition or compression-ignition) excluding free piston engines; - rotary piston engines. These engines may be naturally aspirated or pressure-charged, either using a mechanical pressurecharger or turbocharger. NOTE - This International power correction factors

1b) Except in the case where there is a risk of the system having a noticeable influence upon engine power, an equivalent system may be used. 2) If an exhaust brake is incorporated in tha engine, the throttle valve shall be fixed fully open. / 3) The fuel feed pressure may be adjusted, if necessary, to reproduce tha inlet pump pressure conditions consistent with the particular engina application (particularly where a "fuel return" system, e.g. to tenk or filter, is used), 4) The air inlet valve is the control valve for the pneumati~+governor of the injection pump. 5) The radiator, fan, fan cowl, water pump and thermostat shall be located on the test bed in the same relative positions that they will occupv on tha machine, The cooling liquid circulation shall be operated by the engine water pump onlv. Cooling of the liquid may be produced either bv the engine radiator or bv an external circuit, provided that the pressure loss of this circuit and the pressure at the pump inlet remains substantially the same as those of the engine cooling system. The radiator shutter, if incorporated, shall be in the open position. Where the fan, radiator and cowl svstem cannot conveniently be fitted to the engine, the power absorbed by the fan when separately mounted in its correct position in relation to the radiator and cowl (if used), shall be determined at the speeds correspondingto the engine speeds used for measurement of the engine power either bv calculation from standard characteristics or by practical tests. This power corrected to the standard atmospheric conditions defined in 6.2 shall be deducted from the corrected power. 6) Where a disconnectable or progressive fan or blower is incorporated, the test shall be made with the disconnectable fan or blower disconnected or with the progressive fan running as maximum slip. 7) The thermostat may be fixed in the fully open position.

5.3 Test conditions 5.3.1 The net power test shall consist of a run at full throttle for spark-ignition engines and at fixed full load fuel injection for pump setting compression-ignition engines, the engine being equipped as specified in table 1. 5.3.2 Performance data shall be obtained under stabilized operating conditions with an adequate fresh air supply to the engim. Engines shall have been run-in in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations. Combustion chambers mav contain deposits, but in limited quantitv. Test conditions such as inlet air temperature shall be selected as near to reference conditions (see 6.2) as possible in order to minimize the magnitude of the correction factor. 5.3.3 The temperature of the inlet air to the engine shall be measured within the inlet ductwork. The inlet depression measurement shall be made at the same point. The thermometer or thermocouple shall be shielded from radiant heat and located directly in the air stream. It shall also be shielded from fuel spray-back, A sufficient number of locations shall be used to give a representative average inlet temperature. 5.3.4 The inlet depression shall be measured downstream of the entry ducts, air filter, inlet silencer, speed-limiting device (if they are fitted) or their equivalents. 5.3.5 The absolute pressure at the entrv to the engine downstream of the compressor and heat exchanger, if thev are fitted, shall be measured in the inlet manifold and at any other point where pressure has to be masured to calculate correction factors. The exhaust back pressure shall be 5.3.6 measured at a point at least three pipe diameters from the outlet flanges(s) of the exhaust the manifold(s) downstream of and

Certain machine accessories necessary only for operation of the machine, and which may be mounted on the engine, shall be removed for the test. The following non-exhaustive list is given as an example: - machine hydraulic system(s) pumps; - machine control system(s) hydraulic system pumps; - air compressor for machine svstems; - air-conditioning svstem compressor. Where accessories cannot be removed, the power absorbed by them in the unloaded condition mav be determined and added to the measured engine power. 5.1.3 Compression-ignition auxiliaries engine starting

For auxiliaries used to start compression -ignition cases shall be the two following engines, considered. is fitted and a) Electrical starting: thegenerator supplies, where necessarv, the auxiliaries indispensable to the operation of the engine. b) Starting other than electrical: if there are anv electrically operated accessories indispensable to the operation of the engine, the generator is fitted to supplv these accessories. Otherwise, it is removed. In either case, the system for producing and accumulating the energv necessarv for starting is fitted and operates in the unloaded condition.
